verbatim: It follows from this common-sense definition that the term "system" stands, in general, for a set of some things and a relation among the things.

Symbol T may stand for a single set with arbitrary elements, finite or infinite, but can also represent, for example, a power set (the set of all subsets of another set), any subset of the power set, or an arbitrary family of distinct sets.
Cartesian products provide a basis for defining relations. A relation, in general, is a subset of some Cartesian product of given sets.
